planting.note: Set out nursery starts after frost danger passes into lean, sharply drained soil in full sun; this selection resents soggy winter soil far more than cold, so raised beds or slopes help in heavier Gulf Coast clay.

directions: Heather Queen is a cultivated selection of the Texas and New Mexico native Agastache cana, producing tall wands of dark pink tubular flowers above gray-green, anise-scented foliage from summer into fall. It flowers reliably in its first year from a spring planting and draws hummingbirds steadily through the bloom season. Give it lean, fast-draining soil and full sun; it handles summer heat and drought with ease but needs excellent winter drainage to persist in humid climates. Cut back old flower stems in late winter before new growth emerges.

planting.note: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost, pressing seed lightly into the surface since light aids germination, then transplant into average, well-drained soil in full sun after frost danger passes.

directions: Korean Zest is a compact, bushy form of Korean mint bearing dense violet-blue flower spikes from midsummer through early fall above licorice-mint-scented foliage that can be harvested for tea. Its tidier habit than the species makes it useful in smaller borders or herb gardens without staking. It tolerates average garden soil better than many agastaches and rebounds well after a hard pruning once bloom slows. Bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds all visit the flowers heavily.

planting.note: Surface-sow and press in lightly, since seed needs light to germinate; start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost and transplant into full sun and regular, well-drained soil once frost danger passes.

directions: This white-flowered form of Korean mint, also sold under the UK spelling 'Liquorice White', sends up bottlebrush spikes of pearly white bloom above minty, aromatic foliage from summer through fall, a clean counterpoint to the species' usual violet-blue. It is deer- and rabbit-resistant and draws steady pollinator traffic, including bees and hummingbirds. Give it regular moisture while establishing; mature plants tolerate short dry spells but perform best with consistent watering rather than the bone-dry conditions preferred by desert agastaches. Deadhead spent spikes to extend bloom into fall.

planting.note: A patented sport propagated only from divisions or cuttings, not seed; set out nursery plants after frost danger passes into average, well-drained soil in full sun.

directions: Crazy Fortune arose in a Dutch garden as a variegated sport of 'Blue Fortune' and is grown as much for its leaves as its flowers: each anise-scented leaf carries a grayish-green center streaked with white, giving the whole clump a frosted, variegated look even before the blue-purple flower spikes open in summer. It keeps the hybrid vigor and long bloom season typical of rugosa-type agastaches while adding season-long foliage interest to borders. Because it is a sport rather than a seed strain, named divisions are the only way to keep the variegation true. Full sun and good drainage keep the foliage pattern crisp and the clump from flopping.

planting.note: A patented hybrid grown from divisions or cuttings, not seed; set out nursery plants after frost danger passes into lean, sharply drained soil in full sun.

directions: Pink Pearl is a dwarf hummingbird mint bred by Terra Nova Nurseries for small gardens and containers, staying under two feet tall while covering itself in soft pink tubular flowers from late spring clear into fall, earlier in the season than many taller agastaches. Its mint-scented foliage and compact, mounding habit make it useful at the front of a border where larger hummingbird mints would overwhelm the space. It is drought-tolerant once established and wants excellent drainage above all else, since wet feet are a far greater threat than heat or dry spells. Terra Nova later released the related 'Peach Pearl' as its companion.

planting.note: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost at about 70F until germination, then grow on cooler; transplant into regular to rich, well-drained soil in full sun to part shade after frost danger passes.

directions: Double Diamond produces masses of small, fully double white pompom flowers on wiry stems above narrow, dark green foliage, a more compact and more fully double counterpart to the older cultivar 'The Pearl'. The tidy button blooms are excellent for cutting and hold up well in dried arrangements. Unlike most drought-tough yarrows, this species-group member prefers steadier moisture and will decline in prolonged dry spells, so water during hot stretches rather than treating it as fully xeric. Divide clumps every two to three years in spring to maintain vigor and bloom density.

planting.note: Grown from cuttings or divisions rather than seed; set out nursery plants after frost danger passes into lean to average, well-drained soil in full sun.

directions: Marvelette Blue is a dwarf, mounding form of calamint bred by Walters Gardens to stay compact and tidy, unlike the loose, sprawling habit of the wild species, while still producing the same haze of tiny lavender-blue, mint-scented flowers from early summer well into fall. Its small size suits edging, rock gardens, and containers where standard calamint would flop. It blooms in its first year and tolerates heat, drought, and lean soil once established, needing little more than full sun and good drainage. Pollinators, especially small bees, visit it in large numbers throughout its long bloom season.

planting.note: A patented hybrid propagated only from cuttings or divisions, not seed; set out nursery plants after frost danger passes into well-drained soil in full sun.

directions: Cha Cha Purple is a compact Terra Nova-bred hybrid beardtongue selected for a bushy, well-branched habit and an unusually long bloom season, covering itself in wine-purple tubular flowers from late spring into fall. Its semi-evergreen rosette of foliage holds up through mild winters in warmer zones, and the dense habit needs no staking even in exposed sites. It is drought-tolerant once established and prefers lean, sharply drained soil, since wet winter conditions are far more damaging than cold. Bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds all visit the flowers readily through its long season.
